igcse-0580-time-units.description: Convert between seconds, minutes, hours and calendar units.

examples.title: Convert a duration to minutes
examples.question: A school event lasts 3 h 7 min. Give its duration in minutes.
solution: Count 60 minutes for each of the 3 full hours, giving 180 minutes.

examples.title: Convert a duration to minutes
examples.question: A school event lasts 7 h 11 min. Give its duration in minutes.
solution: Count 60 minutes for each of the 7 full hours, giving 420 minutes.

examples.title: Use the remainder when converting seconds
examples.question: A clip lasts 306 seconds. After recording all full minutes, how many seconds are left?

examples.title: Use the remainder when converting seconds
examples.question: A clip lasts 550 seconds. After recording all full minutes, how many seconds are left?

examples.title: Count full years using the stated convention
examples.question: A plan runs for 1 years and 6 days. Use 365 days per year. Give the duration in days.

examples.title: Count full years using the stated convention
examples.question: A plan runs for 1 years and 10 days. Use 365 days per year. Give the duration in days.

sections.title: How many minutes make up the duration?
sections.label: Minutes
sections.intro: Separate the complete hours from the leftover minutes. Count 60 minutes per hour.

blocks.html: Multiply the hours by 60 and add the extra minutes.

figure.alt: A timeline covering two hours and a further half hour.
figure.caption: Two hours and 30 minutes add to 150 minutes.

blocks.prompt: A school event lasts 4 h 15 min. Give its duration in minutes.
blocks.hint: An hour is 60 minutes.
blocks.solution:
Count 60 minutes for each of the 4 full hours, giving 240 minutes.

Add the extra 15 minutes.

The answer is \(255\).

retry.feedback: Write the hours as groups of 60 minutes before adding the remaining minutes.

blocks.html: The two parts of a duration are in different units.

blocks.prompt: A school event lasts 7 h 18 min. Give its duration in minutes.
blocks.hint: An hour is 60 minutes.
blocks.solution:
Count 60 minutes for each of the 7 full hours, giving 420 minutes.

Add the extra 18 minutes.

The answer is \(438\).

retry.feedback: Write the hours as groups of 60 minutes before adding the remaining minutes.

sections.title: What remains after whole minutes?
sections.label: Seconds
sections.intro: Group seconds in lots of 60. Each full group is one minute.

blocks.html: Keep the number of whole groups and the leftover seconds.

blocks.prompt: A clip lasts 794 seconds. After recording all full minutes, how many seconds are left?
blocks.hint: The remainder must be less than 60 seconds.
blocks.solution:
794 contains 13 whole groups of 60 seconds.

Subtract 780 seconds and keep the remainder.

The answer is \(14\).

blocks.html: The decimal digits of a number of minutes do not tell you the seconds.

blocks.prompt: A clip lasts 977 seconds. After recording all full minutes, how many seconds are left?
blocks.hint: The remainder must be less than 60 seconds.
blocks.solution:
977 contains 16 whole groups of 60 seconds.

Subtract 960 seconds and keep the remainder.

The answer is \(17\).

sections.title: How are days, weeks, months and years related?
sections.label: Days
sections.intro: There are 7 days in a week and 12 months in a year. Use 365 days when the question treats a year as 365 days.

blocks.html: Use the given number of days in a month or read it from a calendar.

blocks.prompt: A plan runs for 1 years and 3 days. Use 365 days per year. Give the duration in days.
blocks.hint: Use the number of days per year stated in the question.
blocks.solution:
Take 1 groups of 365 days.

Add 3 days to the 365 days.

The answer is \(368\).

blocks.html: The months have different lengths.

blocks.prompt: A challenge lasts 6 weeks and 4 days. How many days does it last?
blocks.hint: Convert the weeks before adding.
blocks.solution:
Multiply the 6 weeks by 7 days, giving 42 days.

Include the remaining 4 days.

The answer is \(46\).

extraPractice.solution:

extraPractice.hint: The remainder must be less than 60 seconds.
extraPractice.solution:
1343 contains 22 whole groups of 60 seconds.

Subtract 1320 seconds and keep the remainder.

The answer is \(23\).

extraPractice.hint: The remainder must be less than 60 seconds.
extraPractice.solution:

extraPractice.hint: Use the number of days per year stated in the question.

extraPractice.hint: Convert the weeks before adding.

Include the remaining 6 days.

revision.body:
How many minutes make up the duration?

Multiply the hours by 60 and add the extra minutes.

What remains after whole minutes?

Keep the number of whole groups and the leftover seconds.

Use the given number of days in a month or read it from a calendar.

igcse-0580-time-clocks.description: Convert between clock systems and read the hour and minute hands.

examples.title: Convert a 12-hour reading to 24-hour time
examples.question: Write \(3:06\) a.m. in 24-hour notation.

examples.title: Convert a 12-hour reading to 24-hour time
examples.question: Write \(7:10\) a.m. in 24-hour notation.

examples.title: Convert a 24-hour reading to 12-hour time
examples.question: Write \(09:21\) in 12-hour notation.
solution: Hours below 12 are a.m. Hours from 12 onwards are p.m.
The 12-hour reading uses hour 9 with the same minutes.

examples.title: Convert a 24-hour reading to 12-hour time
examples.question: Write \(13:33\) in 12-hour notation.
solution: Hours below 12 are a.m. Hours from 12 onwards are p.m.
The 12-hour reading uses hour 1 with the same minutes.

examples.title: Read the hour and minute hands
examples.question: It is morning. An analogue clock's minute hand points to 5. Its hour hand has passed 5 and has not reached 6. Write the time in 24-hour notation.
solution: Count 5 groups of five minutes to get 25 minutes.
Use the hour just passed, 5. Between midnight and 1 a.m. the hour is written 00.

examples.title: Read the hour and minute hands
examples.question: It is morning. An analogue clock's minute hand points to 9. Its hour hand has passed 9 and has not reached 10. Write the time in 24-hour notation.
solution: Count 9 groups of five minutes to get 45 minutes.
Use the hour just passed, 9. Between midnight and 1 a.m. the hour is written 00.

sections.title: What time is noon or midnight?
sections.label: To24
sections.intro: The 24-hour clock starts at 00:00. Noon is 12:00. Afternoon times after 12:59 have hour 13 or later.

blocks.html: Convert the hour using a.m. or p.m. Keep the minutes the same.

Name24-hour time
Midnight00:00
Noon12:00
4:15 p.m.16:15

blocks.prompt: Write \(11:14\) a.m. in 24-hour notation.
blocks.hint: The minutes are unchanged. Check the time of day before adjusting the hour.
blocks.solution:
Keep this morning hour.

Keep the minutes at \(14\).

The time is \(11:14\).

blocks.html: The hour for 12 a.m. becomes 00. The hour for 12 p.m. stays at 12.

blocks.prompt: Write \(2:17\) a.m. in 24-hour notation.
blocks.hint: The minutes are unchanged. Check the time of day before adjusting the hour.
blocks.solution:
Keep this morning hour.

Keep the minutes at \(17\).

The time is \(02:17\).

sections.title: When should I write a.m. or p.m.?
sections.label: To12
sections.intro: The 12-hour clock names the half-day. A time from noon onwards uses p.m.

blocks.html: If the 24-hour hour is 13 or more, subtract 12. Read hour 00 as 12 a.m.

blocks.prompt: Write \(17:45\) in 12-hour notation.
blocks.hint: Check which side of noon the hour falls in.
blocks.solution:
Hours below 12 are a.m. Hours from 12 onwards are p.m.

The 12-hour reading uses hour 5 with the same minutes.

The time is 5:45 p.m..

blocks.html: Write both the digits and the a.m. or p.m. label.

blocks.prompt: Write \(14:54\) in 12-hour notation.
blocks.hint: Check which side of noon the hour falls in.
blocks.solution:
Hours below 12 are a.m. Hours from 12 onwards are p.m.

The 12-hour reading uses hour 2 with the same minutes.

The time is 2:54 p.m..

sections.title: Which hand tells me the minutes?
sections.label: Hands
sections.intro: The long hand indicates minutes. It takes five minutes to move from one big number to the next.

blocks.html: Read the hour just passed by the short hand. Count the long hand in fives. At the top the minutes are zero.

figure.alt: Clock with its long hand towards twelve and its short hand towards three.
figure.caption: The minute hand is at zero minutes. The short hand shows three o'clock.

blocks.prompt: It is morning. An analogue clock's minute hand points to 2. Its hour hand has passed 1 and has not reached 2. Write the time in 24-hour notation.
blocks.hint: The short hand shows the hour just passed. The long hand's numbers count in fives.
blocks.solution:
Count 2 groups of five minutes to get 10 minutes.

Use the hour just passed, 1. Between midnight and 1 a.m. the hour is written 00.

The time is \(01:10\).

blocks.html: At half past the hour the short hand is halfway to the next number.

blocks.prompt: It is morning. An analogue clock's minute hand points to 5. Its hour hand has passed 4 and has not reached 5. Write the time in 24-hour notation.
blocks.hint: The short hand shows the hour just passed. The long hand's numbers count in fives.
blocks.solution:
Count 5 groups of five minutes to get 25 minutes.

Use the hour just passed, 4. Between midnight and 1 a.m. the hour is written 00.

The time is \(04:25\).

extraPractice.hint: The minutes are unchanged. Check the time of day before adjusting the hour.

igcse-0580-time-elapsed.description: Find durations and count forwards or backwards on a 24-hour clock.

examples.title: Count forward between two clock readings
examples.question: A session starts at \(23:20\) and finishes at \(00:08\) the next day. Give the duration in minutes.
solution: Then count 8 more minutes to \(00:08\). Add both jumps.

examples.title: Count forward between two clock readings
examples.question: A session starts at \(21:24\) and finishes at \(22:12\). Give the duration in minutes.
solution: Then count 12 more minutes to \(22:12\). Add both jumps.

examples.title: Find the finish time
examples.question: An observation begins at \(22:15\) and lasts 27 minutes. Give its finish time in 24-hour notation.
solution: Convert \(22:15\) to 1335 minutes after midnight. Then add the 27 minutes.
Convert the result back to hours and minutes, moving to the next day if the result reaches 1440 minutes.

examples.title: Find the finish time
examples.question: An observation begins at \(21:19\) and lasts 35 minutes. Give its finish time in 24-hour notation.
solution: Convert \(21:19\) to 1279 minutes after midnight. Then add the 35 minutes.
Convert the result back to hours and minutes, moving to the next day if the result reaches 1440 minutes.

examples.title: Find the start time
examples.question: A workshop must finish at \(23:16\). It lasts 29 minutes. Give its start time in 24-hour notation.
solution: Convert \(23:16\) to 1396 minutes after midnight. Then subtract the 29 minutes.
Convert the result back to hours and minutes, moving to the next day if the result reaches 1440 minutes.

examples.title: Find the start time
examples.question: A workshop must finish at \(22:20\). It lasts 37 minutes. Give its start time in 24-hour notation.
solution: Convert \(22:20\) to 1340 minutes after midnight. Then subtract the 37 minutes.
Convert the result back to hours and minutes, moving to the next day if the result reaches 1440 minutes.

sections.title: How long passes between two readings?
sections.label: Between
sections.intro: Draw a timeline. Jump to the next whole hour, then onwards to the finish.

blocks.html: Add the lengths of the jumps. Continue from 00:00 when crossing midnight.

figure.caption: Count 16 minutes to midnight, then another 27 minutes.

blocks.prompt: A session starts at \(22:28\) and finishes at \(23:16\). Give the duration in minutes.
blocks.hint: Count through the next whole hour. At midnight reset the clock to 00:00.
blocks.solution:
Count from \(22:28\) to \(23:00\): 32 minutes.

Then count 16 more minutes to \(23:16\). Add both jumps.

The answer is \(48\).

blocks.html: The digits on a clock do not form a decimal number.

blocks.prompt: A session starts at \(22:31\) and finishes at \(23:19\). Give the duration in minutes.
blocks.hint: Count through the next whole hour. At midnight reset the clock to 00:00.
blocks.solution:
Count from \(22:31\) to \(23:00\): 29 minutes.

Then count 19 more minutes to \(23:19\). Add both jumps.

The answer is \(48\).

sections.title: How can I find the finish time?
sections.label: Finish
sections.intro: Start at the given time and add the duration. When the minute count reaches 60, make a new hour.

blocks.html: Count forward. After 23:59 the next minute is 00:00 the next day.

blocks.prompt: An observation begins at \(20:23\) and lasts 43 minutes. Give its finish time in 24-hour notation.
blocks.hint: Work from the given time and add the whole duration.
blocks.solution:
Convert \(20:23\) to 1223 minutes after midnight. Then add the 43 minutes.

Convert the result back to hours and minutes, moving to the next day if the result reaches 1440 minutes.

The time is \(21:06\).

blocks.html: Count minutes on the clock in groups of 60.

blocks.prompt: An observation begins at \(23:26\) and lasts 49 minutes. Give its finish time in 24-hour notation.
blocks.hint: Work from the given time and add the whole duration.
blocks.solution:
Convert \(23:26\) to 1406 minutes after midnight. Then add the 49 minutes.

Convert the result back to hours and minutes, moving to the next day if the result reaches 1440 minutes.

The time is \(00:15\).

sections.title: How can I find an earlier start time?
sections.label: Start
sections.intro: Start with the finish and count the duration backwards. If it helps, make jumps to a whole hour.

blocks.html: Subtract the whole duration. Regroup one hour as 60 minutes when needed.

blocks.prompt: A workshop must finish at \(21:24\). It lasts 45 minutes. Give its start time in 24-hour notation.
blocks.hint: Work from the given time and subtract the whole duration.
blocks.solution:
Convert \(21:24\) to 1284 minutes after midnight. Then subtract the 45 minutes.

Convert the result back to hours and minutes, moving to the next day if the result reaches 1440 minutes.

The time is \(20:39\).

blocks.html: Adding a duration to the finish tells you a later time.

blocks.prompt: A workshop must finish at \(19:27\). It lasts 51 minutes. Give its start time in 24-hour notation.
blocks.hint: Work from the given time and subtract the whole duration.
blocks.solution:
Convert \(19:27\) to 1167 minutes after midnight. Then subtract the 51 minutes.

Convert the result back to hours and minutes, moving to the next day if the result reaches 1440 minutes.

The time is \(18:36\).

igcse-0580-time-timetables.description: Read a timetable, choose a service and use a fixed local-time offset.

examples.title: Find the last service before a deadline
examples.question:
StopABC
Museum08:0408:2508:46
Square08:1908:4009:01
Library08:3008:5109:12

What is the latest departure time from the Museum that reaches the Library by \(08:52\)? Use 24-hour notation.
solution: Read along the Library row. Service C arrives after the deadline.
Follow the column for service B back to the Museum row.

examples.title: Apply a fixed time-zone difference
examples.question: Town B is 210 minutes ahead of Town A. It is \(06:16\) in Town A. Find the local time in Town B, in 24-hour notation.
solution: Ahead of means add the time difference.
If the calculation crosses midnight, continue reading the other day's clock.

solution: Ahead of means add the time difference.
If the calculation crosses midnight, continue reading the other day's clock.

sections.title: Which service arrives before the deadline?
sections.label: Deadline
sections.intro: Find the row for the destination, then pick the latest acceptable time. Follow that column back to the start.

blocks.html: The same column shows all the times for one service.

figure.alt: Three service columns, with service B highlighted from top to bottom.
figure.caption: Read down the chosen service column when you compare stops.

blocks.prompt:
StopABC
Museum08:1208:3308:54
Square08:2608:4709:08
Library08:3508:5609:17

What is the latest departure time from the Museum that reaches the Library by \(08:57\)? Use 24-hour notation.
blocks.hint: Choose the service from its arrival, then read its departure.
blocks.solution:
Read along the Library row. Service C arrives after the deadline.

Follow the column for service B back to the Museum row.

The time is \(08:33\).

blocks.html: A later departure is useful only if its arrival still meets the deadline.

sections.title: How long does the journey take?
sections.label: Journey
sections.intro: Read two times from the same service. Check which stop each time belongs to.

blocks.html: Find the duration between the two times using jumps.

Museum08:1308:3508:57
Square08:2808:5009:12

blocks.solution:
Read column C from \(08:57\) to \(09:12\).

Count the minutes between these times.

The answer is \(15\).

Count the minutes between these times.

The answer is \(18\).

sections.title: Which way does a local-time difference go?
sections.label: Zone
sections.intro: When a place is ahead, its clock is later. When it is behind, its clock is earlier.

blocks.html: Add or subtract the offset. Change the day if your result crosses midnight.

blocks.prompt: Town B is 180 minutes ahead of Town A. It is \(14:24\) in Town A. Find the local time in Town B, in 24-hour notation.
blocks.hint: Use the stated direction between the clocks. The difference is not a journey duration.
blocks.solution:
Ahead of means add the time difference.

If the calculation crosses midnight, continue reading the other day's clock.

The time is \(17:24\).

blocks.html: A local-time offset is a difference between clocks. A journey duration is a different quantity.

blocks.prompt: Town B is 270 minutes behind Town A. It is \(17:27\) in Town A. Find the local time in Town B, in 24-hour notation.
blocks.hint: Use the stated direction between the clocks. The difference is not a journey duration.
blocks.solution:
Behind means subtract the time difference.

If the calculation crosses midnight, continue reading the other day's clock.

The time is \(12:57\).

Museum08:2108:4309:05
Square08:3508:5709:19
Library08:4809:1009:32

What is the latest departure time from the Museum that reaches the Library by \(09:11\)? Use 24-hour notation.
extraPractice.hint: Choose the service from its arrival, then read its departure.
extraPractice.solution:
Read along the Library row. Service C arrives after the deadline.

Follow the column for service B back to the Museum row.

The time is \(08:43\).

extraPractice.prompt: Town B is 210 minutes ahead of Town A. It is \(06:34\) in Town A. Find the local time in Town B, in 24-hour notation.
extraPractice.hint: Use the stated direction between the clocks. The difference is not a journey duration.
extraPractice.solution:
Ahead of means add the time difference.

If the calculation crosses midnight, continue reading the other day's clock.

The time is \(10:04\).

extraPractice.prompt: Town B is 240 minutes behind Town A. It is \(07:35\) in Town A. Find the local time in Town B, in 24-hour notation.
extraPractice.hint: Use the stated direction between the clocks. The difference is not a journey duration.
extraPractice.solution:
Behind means subtract the time difference.

If the calculation crosses midnight, continue reading the other day's clock.

The time is \(03:35\).

revision.body:
Which service arrives before the deadline?

The same column shows all the times for one service.

How long does the journey take?

Find the duration between the two times using jumps.

Which way does a local-time difference go?

Add or subtract the offset. Change the day if your result crosses midnight.
revision.checks:
1. Town B is 210 minutes ahead of Town A. It is \(06:16\) in Town A. Find the local time in Town B, in 24-hour notation.

    Answer. \(09:46\)
revision.examTip: A local-time offset is a difference between clocks. A journey duration is a different quantity.

glossary.definition: The time between the start and finish of an event.
The start of a new day, 00:00 on the 24-hour clock.
The time shown by clocks in a given place.
